subject: Integration tooling decision log and next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@nebulatech.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Integration tooling decision log and next steps

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum with the NebulaTech PoC: 

TL;DR: For the PoC we recommend starting with a two-track approach — (A) structured tool/function calling for enterprise business actions (CRUD, billing lookups, ticket creation), and (B) an embeddings + reranker pipeline for semantic search and contextual retrieval. We propose Redwood-hosted models for the first phase and a Dedicated deployment later if throughput needs demand it.

Notes from the call (condensed):
- Integration goals: reduce latency for user-facing flows (<250ms p50 token generation), ensure auditable inputs for regulatory review, and keep per-call cost predictable.
- Expected volume: ~500–1,200 inference requests/day initially, spiking in peak batches.
- Auth: NebulaTech will use Okta for SSO; they want mTLS between their VPC and Private deployment in phase 2.
- Routing: primary region us-west with fallback to us-east.

Proposed PoC scope (2 weeks):
1) SDK setup and auth demo: sample SDK integration (Python/Node) that uses API keys + short-lived tokens.
2) Tool definitions: a JSON schema for allowed tools (name, input schema, required scopes, timeout) and a sandbox tool runner for safe execution.
3) Routing policy: a simple routing rule set (latency-first, cost-aware fallback).
4) Embeddings/re-ranker: demo of semantic retrieval using an embeddings index and a lightweight reranker.

Immediate asks from our side: 
- Please confirm the two preferred tool actions to expose in the PoC (e.g., invoice_lookup, create_support_ticket).
- Share a sample record for the embeddings index (500–1,000 anonymized docs).

I've attached an MVP-integration-checklist and a one-page "tool definitions" draft for your review.

Next steps: 
- You: confirm tools + send sample docs by Mon 26 Apr.
- Us: deliver SDK starter repo, tool-defs, and a stub routing config by Thu 29 Apr.
- Schedule a 30-min technical sync next week (link below).

Thanks — happy to adjust scope if you want a narrower PoC.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.ai

Elena —

Great, thanks for confirming. Short answers to your Qs and a proposed failure-handling approach: 

Parallel vs sequential:
- Redwood runtime supports both patterns. For PoC we recommend a hybrid: run non-dependent, idempotent lookups in parallel (invoice_lookup + query_customer_profile), then feed their outputs into a deterministic reranker or merge function.

Failure modes & recommended handling:
- Tool timeout: operate in two stages — (1) return partial response with a standardized meta field ("tool_status": "timeout") so the UI can show degraded data, and (2) trigger an async retry with a backoff policy if the original request had a high business priority.
- Tool error / exception: sandbox the tool and return sanitized error codes (400/422 for input, 503 for transient infra). Include an operation id so logs correlate across Redwood and NebulaTech.
- Partial data: include provenance headers per result (source, confidence). Reranker should prefer higher-confidence structured outputs.

I'll attach a short draft of a tool definition schema and a sample routing config.

Delivery: we'll push the SDK starter by EOD and ping you when the repo is ready.

cc: Jordan to align on timeline and next commercial steps.

—Priya

Attachment: redwood-tool-definitions.md

Elena / Priya —

Following up with a concise architecture recommendation and the sample tool definition we discussed. See below for the JSON-ish schema we used in the PoC repo. Note: I'm pasting the important parts inline; full files are in the attached .md.

-- redwood tool definition (example) --
name: invoice_lookup
description: Retrieve invoice summary by customer id or invoice number.
input_schema:
  - customer_id: string
  - invoice_number: string
required_scopes: [billing:read]
timeout_ms: 1200
retries: 2
parallel_safe: true
output_examples:
  - {invoice_total: 1249.50, status: "PAID", currency: "USD"}

Execution pattern suggestions:
- For lookups marked parallel_safe: execute concurrently with an aggregate timeout and return per-tool status.
- For non-parallel-safe tools (i.e., those that mutate state) ensure single-threaded execution per customer-id and use optimistic locking.

Routing config (sample):
- primary: us-west-2 (latency)
- fallback: us-east-1 (cost/availability)
- model selection: prefer quantized variant for chat tasks under 256 tokens; fall back to full-fp model for high-quality reranking.

Observability hooks to include for the PoC:
- per-tool latency, success rate, error codes; token-level cost estimate; KV cache hit ratio for embeddings retrieval.

Attachments: sample-routing-config.yaml (small stub)

Happy to walk through this on the technical sync.

-rishi
